note: Re-judged 2026-10-30 (independent judge) after the row's annotation moved from {not-applicable} to {gap}. RFC 1195 Section 1.4 reads 'In a dual area within a dual routing domain only dual routers may be used.' The sentence names no role a not-applicable quote could bind (it carries a lower-case 'may', has the dual area as its subject, and no owner decision declines dual operation), so the earlier not-applicable verdict, which rested on 'binds the network design', no longer stands and the absent dual capability is a conformance gap. Ze is an IP-only Integrated IS-IS router: internal/plugins/isis/lsdb/encode.go::protocolNLPIDs advertises only NLPID 0xCC (IPv4) and 0x8E (IPv6) in the Protocols Supported TLV and never 0x81 (CLNP), and no CLNP forwarding path exists in internal/plugins/isis, so Ze can never be the dual router the sentence requires, and nothing refuses or warns when it is placed in a dual area. No test is tagged to the row.
